title: Exercise Northstar: D-30
description: A major military exercise kicks off in 30 days. Command wants a live screen showing where every unit is, how many supplies they have, and whether their radios are working. Your team builds it from scratch.
storyContext: Your team just got pulled into a classified project. In 30 days, the SAF launches Exercise Northstar — the biggest multi-domain exercise this decade. Command wants one screen showing every unit's position, supplies, and comms status in real time. The catch: it has to work in jungle with barely any mobile signal.

software-engineer.title: Design the Command Screen Layout
software-engineer.instruction: Commanders need one screen showing everything at once. Drag the most critical info to the main display, supporting details to the side panels, and lightweight status to the bottom bar.
software-engineer.hint: What do commanders check every few seconds versus every few minutes? The most urgent info gets the most space.

data-scientist.title: Handle the Data Flow
data-scientist.instruction: Field units send their position every 30 seconds — thousands of updates per minute. How do you turn that into useful info on screen?
data-scientist.hint: You can process each update instantly or collect them in short batches. Think about how much a 5-second delay actually matters versus the risk of showing bad data.

options.label: Process every update the instant it arrives. Screen updates in real time, but needs heavy computing power and one bad reading could glitch the whole display.
Collect updates every 5 seconds, clean them, then display. Positions are at most 5 seconds old and the screen never shows bad data.
Process data on the unit's own device and only send a summary. Cuts radio usage by 80% — crucial in the field — but you lose the detailed raw readings.
Send critical alerts instantly, bundle everything else in 10-second updates. Balanced, but more complex to build and maintain.

cloud-engineer.title: Set Up the Field Network
cloud-engineer.instruction: The exercise area has patchy mobile signal. Set up a reliable network linking field units to the command screen. Arrange the steps.
cloud-engineer.hint: You can't build a reliable network if you don't know where the dead zones are. Survey first, test thoroughly before the exercise starts.

items.label: Walk the training ground to find dead zones and obstacles
Set up portable relay nodes at key positions across the area
Configure a satellite link as backup for when mobile drops completely
Test data speeds from the furthest position back to the command post
Set up automatic switching so devices jump to the best available network
